additions.reason: Source text section ב (line 35) states: 'עִקַּר הַתְּשׁוּבָה הִיא חֲרָטָה, שֶׁמִּתְחָרֵט עַל הָעֲבֵרָה, בְּחִינוֹת (נדרים כב): פֶּתַח חֲרָטָה, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינוֹת פַּתָּח כַּנַּ"ל'. The Rebbe explicitly states that חרטה (regret/repentance) IS a bechina of פַּתָּח — the same patach-concept that is the core of Package 1. The logic: teshuvah's essential act is charatah, and charatah is called 'petach charatah' (the opening of regret) — bechina of patach because it is the act of opening/separating that releases the person from the bound state of sin (where koach and po'al of the sin were fused) back to the potential for holy actualization. Since פַּתָּח is already in Package 1, חרטה should be added as a bechina-node connected to פַּתָּח within Package 1.

additions.reason: Source text section ב (line 25) states: 'וְזֶה הָרוּחַ, שֶׁהוּא הַמְתָּקַת הֶעָשָׁן שֶׁל הַחֲרוֹן אַף, הוּא בְּחִינַת מָשִׁיחַ, בְּחִינַת (איכה ד:כ): רוּחַ אַפֵּינוּ מְשִׁיחַ ה''. The Rebbe explicitly states that the ruach produced by the sweetening of the anger-smoke IS a bechina of Mashiach — the verse 'רוּחַ אַפֵּינוּ מְשִׁיחַ ה'' is quoted to establish this equation. 'הַמְתָּקַת הֶעָשָׁן' (the sweetened-smoke-ruach) = Mashiach. This is a bechina-node for this Torah. The sweetened ruach is the result of the hamtakat charon af that produces the two spirits (Package 1). Mashiach belongs in Package 1 as the name for the ruach produced when anger is properly sweetened — it is the same spirit that then becomes the koach and po'al of actualization. The concept of מָשִׁיחַ as the sweet ruach connects Package 5 (anger/smoke) through the sweetening-transformation to Package 1 (koach-po'al). It belongs in Package 1 as the positive fruit of the transformation.

additions.reason: Source text section א (line 12) states: 'וְיֵשׁ הִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַשֵּׁם, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן בְּחִינוֹת הִסְתַּלְּקוּת, כִּי הַשֵּׁם הוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ'. The Rebbe explicitly states: 'הַשֵּׁם הוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ' (the [divine] name IS the soul). This appears in the context of explaining what 'histalkut of the name' means — it is a bechina of histalkut of the soul, because the name IS the soul. This bechina-equivalence (שֵׁם = נֶפֶשׁ) is stated with explicit bechina-language ('כִּי הַשֵּׁם הוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ'). Since the teaching describes how the tzaddik's name (= soul) can be surrendered as mesirut nefesh (see the cross-reference in the text: 'לקמן סי' רס'), and this is linked to the domain of emet and the tzaddik's spiritual legacy, this node belongs in Package 2 (Emet/Olam Haba). The name/soul equivalence connects to the יַעֲקֹב / אֱמֶת cluster because Jacob's name was his seal (pnei Hashem = pnei Yaakov) and the נֶפֶשׁ-dimension is the conduit through which disciples receive the tzaddik's ruach.
additions.source_quote: יֵשׁ הִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַשֵּׁם, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן בְּחִינוֹת הִסְתַּלְּקוּת, כִּי הַשֵּׁם הוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ

additions.reason: Source text section ה (line 76) states: 'כְּשֶׁהַדִּבּוּר יוֹרֵד בְּמֵצַר הַגָּרוֹן, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם'. The Rebbe explicitly states that 'מֵצַר הַגָּרוֹן' (the narrow passage of the throat) IS a bechina of 'גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם' (the exile of Egypt). This is direct bechina language. The constriction of the throat that prevents speech from flowing freely = Egypt's exile = the condition where nekudot are missing from the otiyot. This concept belongs in Package 3 (שלמות הדבור) because the goroh/throat IS the site of the dibur-problem that Package 3 describes. The 'metzar ha-garov' = 'galut Mitzrayim' bechina-pair should be added as two nodes connected to each other and to the speech-perfection domain. Polarity is neutral: the throat-constriction is not intrinsically evil; it is the condition of incomplete speech that needs rectification.

additions.reason: Source text section ה (line 76) states: 'כְּשֶׁהַדִּבּוּר יוֹרֵד בְּמֵצַר הַגָּרוֹן, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם, אֲזַי הוּא אָנוּס עַל פִּי הַדִּבּוּר'. Galut Mitzrayim IS a bechina of the state where the dibur is stuck in the narrow throat (= the state of incomplete speech that Package 3 describes). The Rebbe uses the verse 'וַיֵּרֶד מִצְרַיְמָה – אָנוּס עַל פִּי הַדִּבּוּר' to establish this bechina: Jacob's descent into Egypt was coerced 'by the word/speech' — meaning the condition of speech-constriction IS the exile. This is a companion-node to מֵצַר הַגָּרוֹן (the two form a bechina-pair) and both belong in Package 3 as the negative/incomplete state of speech that the Torah aims to rectify. Polarity is neutral for the same reason as מֵצַר הַגָּרוֹן.

additions.reason: Source text section ג (line 57) states: 'וְזֶה בְּחִינוֹת: מַלְכוּת – פֶּה, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִשְׁלָמִים אוֹתִיּוֹת הַדִּבּוּר'. The Rebbe states 'מַלְכוּת – פֶּה' (Malkhut = the mouth) as a bechina-concept. The speech-faculty (peh/mouth) through which speech is completed (שלמות הדבור) = a bechina of Malkhut. In the kabbalistic framework Malkhut = the sefirah of speech and the mouth. This is explicit bechina-language. While 'מלכות פה' is a known kabbalistic concept appearing in other Torahs (node_id 'מלכות פה' exists for other references), it is not in the dataset for reference=66. In this Torah's context, 'מלכות פה' connects directly to the actualization (koach→po'al) domain: Malkhut = the mouth = the outlet through which koach becomes po'al via speech. It belongs in Package 1 as the faculty-organ through which the alef-structure's actualization occurs, with a secondary connection to Package 3 (speech perfection).

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Lines 5 and 11 use this as a simile ('כְּמוֹ עֲנָפִים בְּאִילָן') not a bechina statement. The word כְּמוֹ indicates comparison, not identity. Excluded.
Line 34 says 'כְּמוֹ חֲלָלִים שׁוֹכְבֵי קֶבֶר' — simile, not bechina. The Rebbe is paraphrasing the verse to say the wicked are like the dead. Not an explicit bechina-node.

Line 24 says 'עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נַעֲשֶׂה מִמֶּנּוּ בְּחִינַת רוּחַ, דְּהַיְנוּ רוּחַ אֲוִירִי, שֶׁנַּעֲשֶׂה מֵהִתְבָּרְרוּת הֶעָשָׁן'. While this uses bechina language, the node 'רוּחַ אֲוִירִי' is immediately equated in line 25 with 'מָשִׁיחַ' — the Mashiach addition (above) is the more explicit and canonical bechina-node. 'רוּחַ אֲוִירִי' is a descriptive phrase for the same concept. Including Mashiach as the gap-node is sufficient; adding רוּחַ אֲוִירִי separately would be redundant.

The phrase 'פִּי שְׁנַיִם' appears many times as the goal/result in eitza statements, not as a bechina-node equated to another concept's essential nature. Line 3 says 'זֶה בְּחִינַת: וִיהִי נָא פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּרוּחֲךָ אֵלָי' but this is using the verse as proof-text for the preceding concept, not establishing 'פי שנים' as a bechina of another concept. Excluded.

Line 14 mentions 'אִטֵּר יָד' in a parenthetical aside ('מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ זֹאת, אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ מַהוּ אִטֵּר יָד'). This is a rhetorical remark, not a bechina statement. The Rebbe says that whoever understands the two-spirits teaching will understand what 'left-handed' means — it is a hint, not a bechina equation. Excluded.
